proof_policy.statement: Source inspection supports the gaps and reusable implementation observations below. File existence, tool names, schema declarations and test filenames do not prove a working customer journey.

Owner, adult, dependent and other-household authorization proof
Provider failure, retry and replay/idempotency behavior

shared_findings.finding: The central registry exposes calendar, task/chore, grocery, reminder, family and notification primitives. The requested pet, relationship, digital-account, moving, purchase-advisor, inventory, brief and project orchestration tools are not registered. Chore create/assign/complete/list primitives already exist and should be reused.

evidence.observation: Registration combines six imported tool sets.
Tool-name search identifies tasks.createChore, tasks.assignChore, tasks.completeChore and tasks.listOpenChores.
Tool-name search identifies grocery list mutation/read primitives, not product comparison or owned-item checking.

shared_findings.first_safe_slice: Add domain definitions incrementally to the existing registry using the parent foundation; separate reads, proposals, internal writes and approval-controlled side effects.

shared_findings.finding: No exact matches were found for the nine packet-specific feature-flag identifiers in app, lib, components or supabase/migrations. Existing tier gates are not evidence that these rollout contracts are implemented.
shared_findings.first_safe_slice: Map the packet flags to the parent-owned rollout mechanism before enabling each completed workflow.

shared_findings.finding: Several mapped UI handlers write directly through the browser Supabase client. Those handlers do not show the required typed actor-aware domain service, domain-event publication and AgentRun linkage. Workload reassignment is a useful existing server-action exception.

evidence.observation: Manual pet creation inserts through createClient().
Checklist generation inserts move_tasks from the browser.
Project completion updates the row from the browser.
Reassignment resolves user context, scopes the update to the active family and writes audit metadata.

shared_findings.first_safe_slice: Wrap the chosen first customer workflow in a typed server service and connect the parent's authorization, event and run-history contracts; do not replace shared infrastructure within this capability group.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Code queries family pet profiles and care records, supports manual insertion and displays due-date/care recommendations.

evidence.observation: Profile form creates a pet from manually supplied fields.
Care-record form stores kind, date, dose and next-due information.
Recommendations use existing records and species care categories.
Pet-care records lack the required source-document, extraction-confidence and run linkage.

gaps.customer_outcome: A vet record cannot become reviewed, source-linked care facts, appointments and reminders through the mapped workflow.
An owner cannot prepare a scoped, time-limited sitter view through the mapped pet module.
Food/supply replenishment and pet-specific travel coordination are not connected to the pet record workflow.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Import a vet record, confirm the extracted facts and create linked care reminders.
safeguards: Preserve owner/vet medication instructions without model-generated changes.
Require review for ambiguous dates or pet identity.
Use parent-owned actor and run contracts.
later_slices: Supply cadence linked to Shopping and Travel

capabilities.existing_behavior: Code calculates effort-weighted workload, suggests reassignment, applies an audited server-side reassignment and supports chore review/rewards.

evidence.observation: Load uses chore estimates plus fixed task and event weights.
Rebalance selection uses relative load and broad member roles, without calendar availability or chore-specific safety/age inputs.
The action checks family membership and open assignment status; it does not evaluate availability or task-specific eligibility.
Age-aware chore-plan generation exists separately from workload reassignment.

gaps.customer_outcome: A suggested recipient is not checked against actual schedule availability and chore-specific age/safety restrictions.
The next cycle does not learn actual completion duration or expose configurable fairness weights in the inspected balancing engine.
A negotiated swap/request-help lifecycle and registered rebalance/swap tools are missing.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Review and apply a safe, available reassignment with an explanation.
safeguards: Revalidate guardian authority and chore eligibility server-side.
Preserve completed or stale assignments.
Keep weights transparent and configurable.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Dates, gifts and relationship preferences are persisted; a reconnect draft uses contact history and linked communications.

evidence.observation: Reconnect draft builds context from logged interactions and communication summaries.
Inspected interaction read policies authorize household membership rather than private-note ownership.
Relationship-date reads are family-scoped; the mapped surface has no private-note visibility workflow.

gaps.customer_outcome: A member cannot rely on private relationship notes remaining excluded from shared retrieval and drafts through the inspected data model.
Low-frequency, configurable follow-up suggestions lack the required review/dismiss/history and domain-tool lifecycle.
Comprehensive deletion of relationship memory and derived indexes is not established by the inspected handlers.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Store a private interaction note and generate a follow-up using only authorized history.
safeguards: Filter before model context construction.
Never send automatically.
Expose edit/dismiss and configurable frequency.

capabilities.existing_behavior: The existing vault is a document view using secure flags, uploads and signed downloads.

evidence.observation: The route renders FilesHubModule with view=vault.
The work surface queries documents; it does not model digital account ownership or recovery.
No matches for digital_accounts, account_recovery_refs, account_access_policies, digital_estate or the account-directory/password-manager search terms.

gaps.customer_outcome: The household cannot inventory service ownership, users, recovery references and password-manager links in a dedicated account workflow.
Explicit emergency access policy and digital-estate/export instructions are not implemented in the mapped vault surface.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Add safe digital-account metadata and retrieve an authorized recovery checklist.
safeguards: No plaintext password fields.
Encrypt sensitive references and log access.
No provider account changes or implicit emergency bypass.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Conditional checklist templates produce dated tasks; the UI tracks boxes, owners, budgets and progress.

evidence.observation: planTasks excludes existing template keys and calculates dates only for new tasks.
Editing the move updates moves only; it does not update existing task due dates.
Inspected migration adds updated_at triggers, not move-date recalculation.

gaps.customer_outcome: After the move date changes, existing checklist tasks retain their old due dates in the inspected implementation.
Address changes and school/pet/service transitions are generic templates, not derived from the household's actual accounts and providers.
Box contents are text entries rather than canonical inventory links supporting automatic post-move location updates.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Change the move date and safely review/recalculate unfinished dependent tasks.
safeguards: Transactional and idempotent update.
Preserve completed tasks and deliberate overrides.
Do not perform external address changes.
later_slices: Canonical box-item links and post-move verification

capabilities.existing_behavior: Shopping lists persist items; retailer helpers provide search deep links and copyable list handoff without pretending to place orders.

evidence.observation: The primary surface reads grocery lists and items.
Retailer support explicitly provides handoff rather than ordering API execution.

gaps.customer_outcome: No mapped workflow checks whether an owned item meets the need or derives compatibility and budget constraints.
No sourced, timestamped candidate comparison or persisted purchase proposal/ownership outcome is implemented in the mapped shopping surface.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Turn a need into explicit requirements and show whether an owned item already solves it.
later_slices: Provider-backed normalized candidates with source and timestamp
Affiliate disclosure and approved retailer handoff
safeguards: No fabricated compatibility, availability or prices.
No purchase execution in the first slice.
first_safe_slice.provider_readiness: Not inspected or exercised; not classified as BLOCKED.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Manual item/photo capture, nested location paths, loan/warranty tracking and move history are present.

evidence.observation: Query is split into raw whitespace tokens; every token must match a stored field or the item is discarded.
Photo upload stores an image without a candidate extraction/confirmation step.
Inspected item/location policies authorize household membership; no per-item hiding contract is present.
Photo removal clears the form path; this handler does not remove the storage object.

gaps.customer_outcome: The mapped surface cannot hide sensitive items from other household members.
Conversational queries such as 'Where are the passports?' can fail because incidental words and punctuation must match stored fields.
No visual candidate review, confidence/last-confirmed location evidence, or complete photo retention/deletion workflow is present.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Answer an authorized item-location question with stored evidence and last-confirmed state.
safeguards: Filter before search and AI retrieval.
Do not guess a location.
Use storage deletion/retention operations for removed photos.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Briefing generation consumes household domains, displays a deterministic digest and operating-index change recap; a separate home_briefs schema provides daily household snapshots.

evidence.observation: Read cache key is fos_briefing_<type>_<date>, without household or member identity.
Generated data is written under the same unscoped key.
Source queries collect multiple household domains; several select display fields without source record IDs.
Model output uses JSON.parse and broad object checks rather than a strict runtime result schema.
Home brief uniqueness is family/date, not a member-specific brief-item/delivery lifecycle.

gaps.customer_outcome: A cached brief is not keyed to household/member identity or permission state, creating a stale-context reuse risk. Runtime household switching was not exercised.
The generated briefing lacks durable member-specific source/action/dismissal records and permission-aware invalidation.
Per-member category/delivery preferences and delivery logs are not established by the inspected briefing workflow.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Display only the current member's authorized, current-household brief and retain explainable item state.
safeguards: Invalidate on household/member/permission changes.
Runtime-validate model output.
Permission-filter before summarization and retrieval.

capabilities.existing_behavior: Project board, material estimates, budget arithmetic, contractor links and quote comparison are present.

evidence.observation: Scope suggestions match keywords against static templates rather than constructing dependency-aware project phases.
Completion updates home_projects.status and completed_at only.
Inspected schema models projects/materials/quotes but not the required phase, decision, receipt and completion handoff lifecycle.

gaps.customer_outcome: Completing a project does not update home assets, warranties, maintenance schedules or linked receipts.
No dependency-aware phase/task plan or decision/change history is implemented in the mapped project workflow.
Manual quote arithmetic does not establish source-backed quote extraction and structured scope comparison.

first_safe_slice.outcome: Finish a project through a reviewed handoff that updates the home's durable records.
safeguards: Idempotent completion and reversible review where possible.
Retain source evidence and cost assumptions.
Escalate safety-critical/professional work.

recommended_sequence.focus: Tenant/member briefing cache isolation and relationship/inventory visibility.
Server-enforced workload availability and chore eligibility.
recommended_sequence.dependency: Parent-owned authorization plus existing chore and calendar primitives.
Parent-owned typed mutation, idempotency, event and AgentRun contracts.

recommended_sequence.focus: Pet document-to-care workflow, safe account directory, purchase requirements and visual capture.
recommended_sequence.dependency: Parent-owned provenance, ingestion and provider interfaces.
